note: Compliance control ledger. Every rule is quoted or paraphrased from a source in ledger/sources.json and mapped to a concrete control implemented in this repository, so the automation cannot drift out of policy. Status VERIFIED means the wording was read from the official page; every rule was re-read and every cited control re-checked against the code on 2026-11-14 (session bbe4ca47). Controls that did not exist were corrected - see R-01 and R-11. SCOPE NOTE ADDED 2026-11-14 (session 0a697d4a, T27, flag F-29): this ledger is a curated set of the rules that constrain THIS platform's modules - it is NOT a complete restatement of the Program Policies, and it must not be read as one. Ten Participation Requirements that directly bound this platform's own modules were missing and have been added as R-22…R-31; further administrative requirements (§6(a)-(f), (h)-(m), (q), (r), (t), (x) and the Products Statement) are still not individually transcribed. Read the source itself: https://affiliate-program.amazon.com/help/operating/policies

rules.requirement: The Site must clearly and prominently state: "As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases." (or a substantially similar statement previously allowed), on the Site or any other location where Amazon authorizes display or use of Program Content.
rules.citation: Associates Program Operating Agreement, Section 5 - Identifying Yourself as an Associate (re-read 2026-11-14)
rules.implemented_control: every page under this repository's control - the primary dashboard (assets/js/app.js renderers + a static block on each root page), the generated pages/ namespace (tools/build_site.py renders DISCLOSURE into every page) and the companion sites - carries the exact sentence. The deploy gate enforces it twice: tools/validate_data.py::check_disclosure fails any page with rel="sponsored" and no disclosure, and the GitHub Actions step 'No page prints a price and every page discloses' fails the build for each of the root, research-hub/, northstar/, zone2/, affiliate-lab/, pages/ and research-hub/ namespaces. Corrected 2026-11-14: this row previously cited `site/compliance-inject.js`, a file that does not exist in this repository.

rules.requirement: Link-level disclosure must be (1) clear - examples given include "(paid link)", "#ad", "#CommissionsEarned" - and (2) conspicuous, placed near the affiliate link or product review so customers do not have to hunt for it. The disclosure must be made in the same medium as the recommendation (voice, text, or both).
rules.citation: Associates Central help: "Why do I have to identify myself as an Associate?"
rules.implemented_control: content templates place the disclosure block immediately above the first affiliate link on the page; the linter tools/generate_articles.py::lint() raises the DISCLOSURE_POSITION error when the first Amazon affiliate link appears before the disclosure block. Corrected 2026-11-14: this row previously named a function `lint_disclosure_proximity`, which does not exist in the repository - the check lives inside `lint()`.

rules.requirement: A material connection must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously; FTC guidance treats "paid link" adjacent to the link as adequate, states "commissionable link" is probably not a clear disclosure, and treats a disclosure buried in a comment section or at the very end of a long post as not clear and conspicuous.
rules.citation: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking (codified at 16 C.F.R. Part 255)
rules.implemented_control: approved disclosure strings are whitelisted in tools/link_builder.py (DISCLOSURE_OK); the banned string "commissionable link" is on DISCLOSURE_BANNED and fails the lint

rules.requirement: Because prices and availability may change, the Site may only show prices and availability if (a) Amazon serves the link in which that price and availability data are displayed, or (b) the data is obtained via Creators API or PA API under the License.
rules.citation: Participation Requirements, Section 2(b) - General Requirements Applicable to All Special Links
rules.implemented_control: no price cell is populated anywhere on this site; ledger/products.json keeps price/availability blank until a Creators API response is stored with its fetch timestamp (tools/amazon_creators_api.py writes `as_of` and refuses to render without it)

rules.requirement: If prices for a Product are displayed in any comparison format alongside prices from non-Amazon sources, the lowest "new" price on the Amazon Site must be displayed and, if provided, the lowest "used" price.
rules.citation: Participation Requirements, Section 2(b)
rules.implemented_control: comparison template (content/templates/comparison.md.tmpl) reserves a lowest-new and lowest-used column that only renders when a stored Creators API offer record supplies them; otherwise the comparison renders qualitative fields only

rules.requirement: No inaccurate, overbroad, deceptive or otherwise misleading claims about any Product, an Amazon Site, or Amazon's policies, promotions or prices. Limited-time promotion mentions must be removed from the Site as soon as the promotion ends on the Amazon Site.
rules.citation: Participation Requirements, Section 2(b)
rules.implemented_control: tools/generate_articles.py::lint() blocks superlatives, urgency phrasing and unverifiable claim verbs unless the sentence carries an inline `<!--evidence:` reference, and refuses text that claims hands-on use of an unverified product. Limited-time promotion copy carries an `expires_utc` front-matter field: the renderer drops the promotion when that moment has passed and the linter raises PROMO_EXPIRED, so an expired promotion can never reach the publish directory (tests/test_pipeline.py::test_expired_promotion_copy_is_removed_and_linted). Corrected 2026-11-14: this row previously named a function `lint_claims`, which does not exist, and described an `expires_utc` enforcement that had never been implemented - it is implemented now.

rules.requirement: Special Links must use the assigned Associates ID, must be accessed directly from the Site, must include the tag as a URL parameter, and customers must not be encouraged to bookmark Special Links. Content may only be linked to the related Product detail page (or other relevant Amazon page) and not to third-party pages.
rules.citation: Participation Requirements, Section 2(a)-(b)
rules.implemented_control: tools/link_builder.py builds links only from amazon.<tld>/dp/<ASIN>?...&tag=< Associates ID >, validates the tag parameter exists, and rejects any href whose host is not an Amazon marketplace host

rules.requirement: Additional "sub-tag" IDs may be used to monitor and optimize Special Links, but under no circumstances may a sub-tag or any Associates reporting be associated with a specific end user (e.g. dynamically assigning sub-tags to visitors to monitor their behaviour).
rules.citation: Participation Requirements, Section 2(b)
rules.implemented_control: the click model keys campaigns to content page + sub-tag only; tools/redirect_server.py stores no user identifier, no cookie identity, and rejects any sub-tag value that varies per request (SUBTAG_STATIC_RULE)

rules.requirement: Requirement 6 lists offline, email, SMS, MMS and printed material as examples of promotional activity that is NOT expressly permitted, and requires written certification of compliance on request. The same restriction is stated in the Program Policies (Participation Requirements §4), which then expressly permits Special Links in emails, SMS and direct messaging from your social media Sites PROVIDED the communications are solicited (opted into by the recipient) and otherwise compliant.
rules.citation: Participation Requirements, Requirement 6
rules.implemented_control: distribution channels in the campaign config are limited to `web` and `approved_mobile_application`; email/SMS channel enum values are absent from the schema. This is deliberately STRICTER than the policy: solicited email/SMS is permitted by Program Policies §4, but this repository's default is web-only and it has no opt-in list, so an unsolicited send could not be shown compliant. The stricter default is a project choice, not an Amazon requirement (F-25).
rules.note: Corrected 2026-11-14 (session a133aa61) after re-reading both pages live. An earlier revision had restated the policy's permission as a prohibition; that is now separated into the requirement text above and labelled as a self-imposed default in the control.

rules.requirement: Content may not be altered - no adding information, no inserting words into a customer review; images may be resized keeping proportions and text may be truncated only where meaning is not materially altered or made misleading. Content may not be sold, resold, redistributed, sublicensed or transferred.
rules.citation: Participation Requirements, Requirements 8 and 9
rules.implemented_control: API-fetched fields are stored in an immutable `raw` block keyed by response hash; templates interpolate them verbatim and the render step fails if a whitelisted field is edited (tools/amazon_creators_api.py::FIELD_IMMUTABILITY)

rules.requirement: The Site must not include any Amazon trademark, or a variant or misspelling of one, in any domain name, subdomain, in any "tag" or Associates ID, or in any username, group name or other identifier on a social networking site. Sites that promote or contain certain content categories are unsuitable for the Program.
rules.citation: Participation Requirements, Section 1 - Enrollment and Eligibility, unsuitable-Sites item (g) (re-read 2026-11-14)
rules.implemented_control: the site is named "Zone2" (tools/build_site.py and tools/validate_data.py SITE_NAME), which contains no Amazon mark. tools/validate_data.py::check_marks fails the build if the site name or the configured Associates tag contains amazon/amzn/prime/kindle, fails affirmative endorsement claims, and raises a review note when a page title leads with a mark (F-13). Corrected 2026-11-14: this row previously named a function `assert_no_amazon_marks` that does not exist; the implemented function is `check_marks`. The site name was changed from "Northstar" to "Zone2" on 2026-11-14 by the final integration, because "Northstar" is the name of the preserved earlier prototype kept at northstar/; the mark check is unaffected.

rules.requirement: The Site must contain original content and be publicly available at the address supplied in the application; original content that uses third-party materials must add significant commentary, analysis, or transformation.
rules.citation: Participation Requirements, Section 1 - Enrollment and Eligibility
rules.implemented_control: every generated article requires `analysis` front matter (non-empty editorial reasoning) before it can publish; pure API-field dumps are rejected by the linter

rules.requirement: A Qualifying Purchase accrues within a Session that begins when a customer clicks a Special Link and ends at the first of: 24 hours elapsing, the customer placing an order for a non-digital Product, or the customer clicking another Associate's Special Link. Cart-adds must complete no later than 89 days after the click-through; Digital Products are counted when streamed/downloaded; and within 180 days of purchase the Product must be shipped/streamed/downloaded and paid for.
rules.citation: Commission Income Statement, Section 1 - Qualifying Purchases and Qualifying Revenue
rules.implemented_control: the revenue model's expected-value function only claims credit inside the 24h window, uses a 89-day cart tail for the delayed-conversion term, and discounts by an assumed-not-observed ship-complete factor of 1.0 until Associates reports exist (no fabricated refund rate)

rules.requirement: Associates' tags should only be used to benefit from Amazon Associates commissions; claiming commissions from both Amazon Associates and another program using the same traffic (e.g. by manipulating or combining attribution links) can lead to withheld commissions and termination.
rules.citation: Commission Income Statement, Section 5 - Commission Income Limitations
rules.implemented_control: tools/link_builder.py rejects a URL that already contains a competing network attribution parameter, and the redirect endpoint refuses chained third-party attribution params

rules.requirement: Commission Income is calculated per Qualifying Purchase and paid approximately 60 days after the end of the calendar month in which it was earned; US payment minimums are 10 USD (direct deposit), 10 USD with a 2000 USD maximum (gift card), and 100 USD with a 15 USD fee (check).
rules.citation: Commission Income Statement, Section 6 - Commission Income Reporting and Payment
rules.implemented_control: cash-flow model in tools/optimize.py uses a 60-day lag and shows the pay-period gate; no earnings figure is displayed on the site without a report row

rules.requirement: Violation of the Agreement (and any violation of Section 5 or the Program Policies, which is deemed a material breach) can lead Amazon to permanently cease payment of commission income, suspend the account, or terminate on 7 days' notice.
rules.citation: Operating Agreement, Sections 2, 5 and 6
rules.implemented_control: the deploy gate (tools/validate_data.py) is a hard pre-publish check: a page that fails the disclosure, naming, or sourcing lint blocks the Pages workflow rather than shipping

rules.requirement: Google asks sites participating in affiliate programs to qualify affiliate links with rel="sponsored", whether created manually or dynamically; failing to qualify affiliate links appropriately can lead to manual actions and algorithmic action affecting how the site is seen in Search.
rules.citation: Google Search Central - Qualify your outbound links to Google; and the Search Central blog on qualifying links
rules.implemented_control: tools/link_builder.py always emits rel="sponsored nofollow" on SponsoredLinks; validate_data.py fails the build if an href to an Amazon host lacks it

rules.requirement: Editorial product reviews can expose pros and cons to Google through Product/Review structured data (positiveNotes / negativeNotes as ItemLists whose text matches the visible page), the review author must be a valid Person or Team name, and Google warns against putting promotional text such as "50% off on Black Friday" in review markup.
rules.citation: Google Search Central - Merchant listing (Product, Offer) structured data
rules.implemented_control: content/templates/*.tmpl emit Product+Review JSON-LD only from verified fields, keep the author name a real Person/Team value, and the linter rejects promotional strings and markup text that is not present visibly

rules.requirement: Amazon makes no representation or warranty regarding the amount of traffic or commission income an Associate can expect, and will not be liable for actions taken based on expectations.
rules.citation: Operating Agreement, Section 4 - Warranties
rules.implemented_control: every projection in this repository is labelled ILLUSTRATIVE and is computed by the documented formula from the operator's own assumptions; no revenue forecast is presented as an Amazon figure

rules.requirement: Product catalog data is obtained through the Creators API (PA-API 5.0 is deprecated and returns 403 AccessDenied). Prerequisites per Amazon's docs: enrolment in the Associates program for the target marketplace, at least 10 qualifying sales within the past 30 days, API registration through Associates Central, and generated credentials.
rules.citation: PA-API 5 Deprecation Notice (creatorsapi/docs/en-us/paapiv5-deprecation) + Creators API introduction, Prerequisites (re-read 2026-11-14)
rules.implemented_control: tools/amazon_creators_api.py targets the Creators API operations (SearchItems, GetItems, GetVariations, GetBrowseNodes) and exits with a machine-readable BLOCKED reason when credentials or the qualifying-sales gate are absent, instead of falling back to scraping

rules.requirement: The Site must not make inaccurate, overbroad, deceptive or otherwise misleading claims about any Product, an Amazon Site, or any of Amazon's policies, promotions, or prices. A headline count that disagrees with the register it summarises is such a claim.
rules.citation: Participation Requirements §2(b) (no inaccurate, overbroad, deceptive or misleading claims)
rules.implemented_control: tools/validate_data.py::check_flag_count compares CANONICAL_FLAG_COUNT in assets/js/data.js against ledger/flags.json and fails the build on any disagreement; the count is rendered from the constant, never typed into markup.

rules.requirement: Unless otherwise agreed by Amazon, your Site must not have price tracking and/or price alerting functionality.
rules.citation: Associates Program Policies — Participation Requirements, Section 6(y) — read 2026-11-14
rules.implemented_control: NO CONTROL IMPLEMENTED - and none is needed yet, because module M-03 (Pricing analysis) is BLOCKED: no API credentials and no cached offer records exist, so nothing on this site tracks a price. This row exists as a DESIGN CONSTRAINT on M-03, whose stated purpose is to 'track price point, discount depth and offer shape per ASIN'. Building that as a tracked time series or an alert would breach §6(y); the permitted reading is a point-in-time offer record fetched from the Creators API and displayed with its as_of timestamp, which is exactly what tools/amazon_creators_api.py writes. The constraint is now listed on pages/modules/m-03-pricing-analysis.html alongside R-04 and R-05.

rules.requirement: You will not use a link shortening service, button, hyperlink or other ad placement in a manner that makes it unclear that you are linking to an Amazon Site.
rules.citation: Associates Program Policies — Participation Requirements, Section 6(w) — read 2026-11-14
rules.implemented_control: tools/link_builder.py::build_product_link rejects any marketplace not in MARKETPLACE_HOSTS and emits only the direct form https://<marketplace>/dp/<ASIN>?tag=... , so no published affiliate link passes through a shortener. tools/link_builder.py::audit_html walks every <a href> in built output and flags an Amazon-host link that lacks rel="sponsored". RELEVANT TO THE SUPPLIED LINKS: the three brief links are themselves short links (link.amazon/<code>); this repository publishes them only as evidence rows on the Products and Verification pages, never as the affiliate link in content, and each is labelled with its resolved destination (F-04, F-24).

rules.requirement: You will not cloak, hide, spoof, or otherwise obscure the URL of your Site containing Special Links (including by use of Redirecting Links) or the user agent of the application in which Program Content is displayed or used such that we cannot reasonably determine the site or application from which a customer clicks through such Special Link to an Amazon Site.
rules.citation: Associates Program Policies — Participation Requirements, Section 6(v) — read 2026-11-14
rules.implemented_control: PARTIAL. The click tracker tools/redirect_server.py exists but is not wired into any published page; when used it resolves a static campaign key from ledger/campaigns.json and redirects, and it stores no visitor identifier (PER_VISITOR_TOKENS are rejected from sub-tags). There is no code that rewrites or hides the referring URL or the user agent. Separately, tools/amazon_creators_api.py sends an identifying 'Agent/[name]' user agent rather than masking it, which is the IP License §4 requirement (tracked as R-07 in this ledger's agent-terms row). The gap: nothing enforces this at deploy time.

rules.requirement: You will not offer any person or entity any consideration, reward, or incentive (including any money, rebate, discount, points, donation to charity or other organization, or other benefit) for using Special Links. For example, you cannot implement any "rewards" or loyalty program that incentivizes persons or entities to visit an Amazon Site via your Special Links.
rules.citation: Associates Program Policies — Participation Requirements, Section 6(g) — read 2026-11-14
rules.implemented_control: NO CONTROL IMPLEMENTED - there is no rewards, loyalty, cashback or referral-incentive code in this repository, so there is nothing to constrain. Recorded as a build-time constraint: the campaign schema in ledger/campaigns.json carries no incentive field, and adding one would be the point at which a lint rule would be required.

rules.requirement: You will not artificially generate clicks or impressions on your Site or create Sessions on an Amazon Site, whether by way of a robot or software program or otherwise.
rules.citation: Associates Program Policies — Participation Requirements, Section 6(s) — read 2026-11-14
rules.implemented_control: PARTIAL, and the relevant control is the agent-transparency one rather than a traffic filter: tools/amazon_creators_api.py identifies itself as 'Agent/[name]' in the user agent and refuses to defeat CAPTCHAs or other human-check measures (IP License §4). No automation in this repository clicks its own Special Links or opens Amazon pages to create Sessions. There is no bot-traffic detector, and this repository does not run a live site, so no such detector is currently needed.

rules.requirement: You will not directly or indirectly purchase any Product(s) or take a Bounty Event action through Special Links, whether for your use or for the use of any other person or entity, and you will not permit, request or encourage any other person or entity to do so. Further, you will not purchase any Product(s) through Special Links or take a Bounty Event action for resale or commercial use (of any kind) or offer any Products on your Site for resale or commercial use of any kind.
rules.citation: Associates Program Policies — Participation Requirements, Section 6(u) — read 2026-11-14
rules.implemented_control: NO CONTROL IMPLEMENTED - this is an operating rule for the site owner, not something code can enforce, because no Associates account exists (F-07) and no Special Link has been published (every product link on this site is an untagged preview_link with a 'NO_TAG - NOT FOR PUBLICATION' warning). Recorded because the bounty rows on pages/commissions.html enumerate Bounty Events: the operator must not trigger them.

rules.requirement: You will not frame an Amazon Site, or any part of it, within your Site, including by display within an integrated web browser (e.g., WebView) within a Mobile Application. However, displaying a Special Link on your Site in accordance with Section 2 of these Participation Requirements, will not be a violation of this section.
rules.citation: Associates Program Policies — Participation Requirements, Section 6(n) — read 2026-11-14
rules.implemented_control: SATISFIED BY ABSENCE AND BY STRUCTURE. Every page in this repository is static HTML with no <iframe>, no embedded WebView and no Amazon-hosted frame; product links open in a new tab (tools/link_builder.py::SponsoredLink.to_html emits target="_blank" with referrerpolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade"). No lint rule is implemented specifically for this row.

rules.requirement: You will not post or serve any Special Links or other content promoting an Amazon Site within any pop-up or pop-under windows, transitional page ads, or layer ads, except for pop-up windows in conjunction with your Site promoting Products closely associated with the materials on your Site.
rules.citation: Associates Program Policies — Participation Requirements, Section 6(o) — read 2026-11-14
rules.implemented_control: SATISFIED BY ABSENCE. No page in this repository contains a pop-up, pop-under, transitional page ad or layer ad; the generated pages are static document flow produced by tools/build_site.py. The site uses no interstitial at all. No lint rule is implemented specifically for this row.

rules.requirement: You will not include any Special Links in any content that you place on an Amazon Site (for example, in connection with any advertising service available through an Amazon Site or in a customer review, forum, Wish List, guide, or any other customer-generated context available on an Amazon Site).
rules.citation: Associates Program Policies — Participation Requirements, Section 6(p) — read 2026-11-14
rules.implemented_control: SATISFIED BY SCOPE. This repository publishes only to this repository's own GitHub Pages origin; nothing here posts content onto an Amazon Site. tools/link_builder.py::audit_html only inspects HTML this project builds, and tools/generate_articles.py writes drafts into content/ for publication on the operator's own site, never to an Amazon surface.

rules.requirement: You will not display on your Site, or otherwise use, any Program Content to advertise or promote any products that are offered on any site that is not an Amazon Site (e.g., products offered by other retailers). You will not display on your Site or otherwise use any data, images, text, or other information or content you may obtain from us that relates to Excluded Products.
rules.citation: Associates Program Policies — Participation Requirements, Section 6(z) — read 2026-11-14
rules.implemented_control: PARTIAL. tools/link_builder.py::build_product_link accepts only hosts in MARKETPLACE_HOSTS, so no Special Link in generated content points at a non-Amazon retailer, and tools/validate_data.py fails the build if an Amazon-host href lacks rel="sponsored". The gap: there is no enforcement that an article never mentions or links a competing retailer alongside Program Content, and no Excluded-Products filter.

coverage_note: Recorded 2026-11-14 by session 0a697d4a (T27). R-22…R-31 were added after a row-by-row re-read of Participation Requirements §6 found them absent. They were chosen because each one constrains a module this repository actually defines in ledger/modules.json - R-22 in particular reverses the expected shape of M-03 (Pricing analysis), which is described as tracking 'price point, discount depth and offer shape per ASIN' while §6(y) forbids price-tracking and price-alerting functionality. Rows still absent from this ledger (§6(a)-(f), (h)-(m), (q), (r), (x)) remain absent; they are not reproduced here because transcribing the governing document in full is not this project's purpose and Amazon's pages are the authoritative source.
